persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
Bora Özkent's day was shaped by the Alphabet and Amazon earnings and the software selloff. **Alphabet** fell about 13% even though cloud revenue grew 108%, as ad growth slowed; Bora calls it an overreaction and says "Google has become quite cheap, in my view." With **ServiceNow** down 27% and **Fortinet** down 21%, he says AI has started to pressure software and cybersecurity companies and expects similar earnings reactions.

He calls hardware "free" and says he is almost fully invested (0.48% cash) and up about 130% this year. He says the only real risk is credit spreads and data-center financing, and thinks an end to the war would ease it. He says he will never sell part of his **Bitcoin** and points to roughly $150-200 thousand for the rest.

items.title: Ne Olacak Bu Piyasaların Hali?
items.summary: In an open livestream, Bora Özkent covered the Alphabet and Amazon earnings and the software selloff. Alphabet's cloud revenue grew 108% while ad growth stayed at 12% (13% expected) and cash flow turned negative; the stock fell about 13%, which Bora calls an overreaction, saying "Google has become quite cheap, in my view." He ties ServiceNow's 27% and Fortinet's 21% drops to AI pressure on software, expects similar earnings reactions and thinks cybersecurity pricing is near its end. He calls hardware "free" and says it will rebound once financing fears fade. He describes GPU rental prices up 11.2% for B300 and 14.7% for H200 over the past month, with agents driving demand. He says Anthropic reached operating profit and positive free cash flow and that closed-model token prices are rising. He says US employment will weaken while the economy grows, which will confuse the Fed. He sees the only real risk as deteriorating credit spreads and data-center financing; an end to the war would ease it. He is almost fully invested (0.48% cash), up about 130% this year, and not changing his stance. He says he will never sell part of his Bitcoin and might sell the rest around $150-200 thousand.

assets.note: Cloud revenue grew 108% with ad growth at 12%; calls the drop excessive and says it has "become quite cheap."
Stock fell 27%; forward sales contracts are shrinking as AI absorbs budgets.
